Welcome to "Ready Before Run(): A Practical Guide to Gear Up for Data Science." This guide is designed for readers from diverse backgrounds — economists, statisticians, engineers, scientists, and beyond — who are interested in producing advanced analytics workflows, but don't necessarily have any computer science foundations.

If you've found this resource, you likely already possess strong analytical skills from your domain. What you may lack is familiarity with the technical infrastructure that supports modern data science work.

This guide walks you through setting up a data science environment — programming languages, version control, visualisation tools, cloud platforms. By the end of it you'll have a working technical foundation.

This is edition {{< var version >}}. The tools change, so the book is revised to keep up, and the [Changelog](chapters/changelog.qmd) lists what each edition changed.

# Preface

The idea for this book goes back to before AI assistants were part of the job, to when the Harvard Business Review called data scientist the "sexiest job of the 21st century" [@davenport2012]. Much has changed since, and it is fair to ask whether data scientists still matter. My view is that AI makes understanding the mechanics of data science more important. Machines may remove much of the grunt work that so many have been well paid for in and around the 2010s. But if we can't tell what the machines are doing, we can't use what they hand back or ask them precisely for what we need, and then we have no basis on which to stay useful in our fields.

This book grew out of my experience as an analyst. There are many resources teaching statistical methods, machine learning algorithms, and data manipulation techniques, and relatively few on the setup that makes that work possible.

"Ready Before Run()" is my attempt at filling that gap: practical guidance for getting a data science workspace standing. We'll sort the environment out first, so you have somewhere solid to work from before you take on anything analytical.

My hope is that this book lowers the technical barriers and leaves you with a foundation you can build on.

Ready? Let's gear up for data science.
